findings.recommendation: Set `sourcemap: false` for release builds in extension/vite.config.ts:47 and extension/scripts/build.mjs:73 (or gate it on the `development` mode the dev script already passes), and add a `.map` and `store/` filter to the archiver call in extension/scripts/package.mjs:53. Better: move extension/public/store/ out of publicDir entirely, e.g. to extension/store-assets/, so Vite never copies it.

findings.title: The server config module lands in the root-layout client chunk, carrying dead process.env.SMTP_PASS and BROWSERBASE_API_KEY reads into every page's JavaScript
findings.description: lib/config/constants.ts (787 lines) re-exports lib/config/config-values.ts (1,367 lines) and is imported directly by client components across the app, including ones mounted in app/layout.tsx. The compiled result is visible in the committed build: static/chunks/9711-3989d97c24edd68e.js, 18 KB and part of the /layout entry (so present on all 311 routes), contains `i.env.SMTP_HOST, i.env.SMTP_PORT, i.env.SMTP_USER, i.env.SMTP_PASS, i.env.SMTP_FROM||i.env.SMTP_USER;` and `i.env.BROWSERBASE_API_KEY&&i.env.BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID;` as bare expression statements alongside the team-role matrix and the API route table. No secret is disclosed: `i` is Next's client process shim and only NEXT_PUBLIC_-prefixed variables are inlined, so these evaluate to undefined -- but the code and the variable names ship, and every unused constant webpack cannot prove dead ships with them.
findings.impact: Every page in the app carries a slice of the server configuration module and dead environment reads for SMTP credentials and the Browserbase API key. It is bytes and noise today, and it is one careless `NEXT_PUBLIC_` rename away from becoming a real disclosure, since the read sites are already compiled into a client chunk.
findings.recommendation: Enforce the split the project already documents in CLAUDE.md: keep lib/config/client-constants.ts as the only module client components import, move the process.env-reading blocks (EMAIL_CONFIG and the Browserbase configured check in lib/config/constants.ts) into a server-only module marked with `import "server-only"`, and change the client-side imports of @/lib/config/constants over to the client-safe module.

findings.title: finalizeScanSuccess acquires a second pool connection from inside its own open transaction, which can deadlock the pool when several scans finish together
findings.description: `finalizeScanSuccess` takes a client with `pool.connect()` (lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:221), opens a transaction (line 237), and inside it calls `saveAutoTags(scanId, txUserId, findings, client)` at line 287. `saveAutoTags`'s first statement is `await loadPromotedRules()` (lib/tags/auto-tags.ts:794), which on a cache miss runs `pool.query(...)` against the module-level pool (lib/tags/auto-tags.ts:720) -- a second connection requested while the first is still held in an open transaction. The rules cache has a 5-minute TTL (lib/tags/auto-tags.ts:702) and is also invalidated on every admin promotion, so misses are real, not theoretical.
findings.impact: With `CONFIG_DB_POOL_MAX = 10`, if ten scans finalize within the same cache-miss window every one of them holds a transaction client and waits for an eleventh connection that cannot exist. All ten stall until `connectionTimeoutMillis` fires and the scans are marked failed after their work was already done.
findings.recommendation: Call `loadPromotedRules()` before `pool.connect()` in lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:221 and pass the resolved rules into `saveAutoTags`, or have `saveAutoTags` run `loadPromotedRules` on the `executor` client it was handed rather than on the global pool (lib/tags/auto-tags.ts:720).

findings.title: Three completion paths write rows one INSERT at a time where a single multi-row INSERT would do: crawl pages, AI verify verdicts, and boot-time migrations
findings.description: (a) At the end of a crawl, `for (const pr of pageResults)` runs one `INSERT INTO scan_history (...) VALUES ($1...$12) RETURNING id` per page (lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:630-650) -- up to 250 sequential round trips on the Elite plan (lib/billing/crawl-page-limits.ts:23). (b) `lib/ai/verify-findings.ts:583-593` loops the verdict map and runs one `INSERT INTO scan_finding_feedback ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` per finding, routinely 50-300 sequential inserts. (c) Boot-time passes do the same: lib/billing/staff-plan.ts:265-268 (one query per staff row, driving SELECT at :254 unbounded), lib/auth/security-migration.ts:89-98 and :123-139 (one UPDATE per row), lib/uploads/avatar-migration.ts:120-151 and :194-214 (three queries per avatar). Note the correct pattern already exists in this codebase: `saveAutoTags` builds a single multi-row INSERT (lib/tags/auto-tags.ts:802-816).
findings.impact: (a) adds 250 serialized round trips to the tail of a crawl the user is already waiting on. (b) adds one round trip per finding to the AI verify flow. (c) lengthens every process start, which matters because instrumentation.ts also runs the full schema DDL at boot.
findings.recommendation: Replace each loop with one multi-row `INSERT ... VALUES (...),(...) RETURNING id` built the way lib/tags/auto-tags.ts:802-816 builds its parameter list, or with `UNNEST($1::type[], ...)` for the larger sets. For (c), a single `UPDATE ... FROM (VALUES ...)` replaces the per-row loops.

findings.title: webhook_deliveries is written on every webhook event and never pruned, because lib/database/cleanup.ts has no retention rule for it
findings.description: `lib/webhooks/delivery.ts:111` inserts a row into `webhook_deliveries` on every delivery attempt (and the module retries once on failure, so a failing webhook writes two rows per event). The table is created at instrumentation.ts:2328 with `idx_webhook_deliveries_webhook_id ON webhook_deliveries(webhook_id, attempted_at DESC)` (:2336). Grepping lib/database/cleanup.ts for `webhook_deliveries` returns nothing -- the retention pass that prunes sessions, rate_limits, tokens, scan_finding_feedback, user_notifications, github_review_usage, ai_conversations, email_logs, system_error_logs and admin_audit_log has no rule for it. AUDIT-011's drift-25 already noted this table has no reader; combined with no writer-side retention, it accumulates forever.
findings.impact: A user with an active webhook on an hourly schedule writes ~24 rows a day per webhook, permanently. Nothing reads the table, so the growth is invisible until it shows up as disk usage and as backup/restore time on the self-hosted deployments this project targets.
findings.recommendation: Either add a retention DELETE for `webhook_deliveries` to lib/database/cleanup.ts alongside the other log tables (with an admin-configurable retention setting matching the pattern used for email_logs), or, if AUDIT-011's drift-25 conclusion holds and the table genuinely has no consumer, stop writing it in lib/webhooks/delivery.ts:111 and drop it.

findings.title: Two per-request lookups sit on the admin engine-feedback page that each pull every findings blob for a tag with no LIMIT
findings.category: N+1 with an unbounded inner query
findings.description: `for (const row of counts.rows)` at app/api/v3/admin/engine-feedback/ai-tag-candidates/route.ts:171 puts a `Promise.all` inside the loop (line 172), so the loop itself is fully sequential -- two round trips per candidate tag. The second of those (lines 182-186) is `SELECT sh.findings FROM scan_tags st JOIN scan_history sh ON sh.id = st.scan_id WHERE st.tag = $1 AND st.source = 'ai'` with no LIMIT: it pulls the complete findings JSONB of every scan carrying that tag and then flatMaps the result in JavaScript at line 191.
findings.impact: Staff-only and low frequency, so bounded in blast radius, but the page cost grows with total AI-tagged scan volume and each iteration transfers (scans with that tag) x (full findings blob) bytes. It is the same shape as perf-06's top-vulnerabilities query and will fail the same way at scale.
findings.recommendation: Hoist the `Promise.all` outside the loop so the per-tag queries actually run in parallel, add a `LIMIT` and a recency bound to the query at line 182, and project only the finding fields the candidate scoring reads rather than `sh.findings` whole.

findings.title: 117 of the 155 API routes bypass the ApiResponse/withErrorHandling helpers and hand-roll five different error body shapes
findings.description: lib/api/api-utils.ts already provides the canonical pieces: ApiResponse (:13-65) emits `{ error, status }` with a matching HTTP status for every 4xx/5xx class, and withErrorHandling (:263-274) converts an uncaught throw into `console.error("[API Error]", error)` plus a fixed `"An unexpected error occurred"` 500. Only 38 of the 155 route.ts files under app/api reference either one; the other 117 build responses with bare NextResponse.json, and 47 route files contain no `catch` at all. The result is five distinct error shapes in production: `{ error }` (bare NextResponse.json, the majority of the 233 `error:`-keyed literals), `{ error, status }` (ApiResponse), `{ success: false, error }` (21 occurrences, e.g. app/api/v3/webhooks/route.ts:299-303 and app/api/v3/stripe/setup-products/route.ts:148-152), `{ error, details, statusCode }` (app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:287-294), and `{ message }` (app/api/v3/teams/members/route.ts:298). The shared client only understands one of them: lib/api/client.ts:46-49 reads `errorData.error` and otherwise falls back to the literal string `API error: <status>` set at :44, so a `{ message }` response surfaces to the user as "API error: 400".
findings.impact: Client code cannot render a reliable message without knowing which route it called, which is how bare status strings end up in front of users. The 47 handler-less routes also mean an unexpected throw is formatted by Next.js rather than by the app, so those responses do not carry the `{ error }` key the client expects at all.
findings.recommendation: Adopt ApiResponse as the single error constructor and wrap every handler in withErrorHandling. Do it in batches by directory rather than one sweep. Start with the five shape outliers named above so the client's single `errorData.error` read in lib/api/client.ts:46 is always satisfied.

findings.title: no-floating-promises is scoped to four auth path globs, so 86 no-op .catch handlers and 8 empty catch blocks in the scanner, billing and webhook paths pass lint
findings.description: eslint.config.mjs's type-aware block enables `@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises` (:126) and `no-misused-promises` (:122) only for the four globs listed at :108-113 (`lib/auth/**/*.ts`, `app/api/v3/auth/**/*.ts`, `app/api/v3/account/**/*.ts`, `app/api/v3/admin/**/*.ts`), and the main rules block (:58-92) enables no rule against empty catch blocks. A scan of the 965 source files under app/, lib/, components/, extension/src/, cli/ and scripts/ finds 8 statement-level `catch {}` blocks with a genuinely empty body, 183 with only a comment, and 86 inline `.catch(() => {})` / `.catch(() => null)` no-op handlers. Most of the 183 are deliberate and documented (a scanner check whose DNS lookup failing genuinely means no finding), which is exactly why the raw count is not itself the finding: the finding is that nothing distinguishes the deliberate ones from the ones filed above as obs-01 and obs-06, and nothing stops the next one being added.
findings.impact: The swallowed-error findings in this section (obs-01 in the scan engine, obs-06 in metering and quota refunds) all live in directories the lint rules do not cover, and none of them would be flagged today. The pattern reproduces on every new file in lib/scanner, lib/billing, lib/webhooks and lib/email.
findings.recommendation: Extend the type-aware `files` list in eslint.config.mjs:108-113 to include `lib/billing/**/*.ts`, `lib/webhooks/**/*.ts`, `lib/email/**/*.ts` and `lib/scanner/*.ts` (the orchestration files, not the 4000-line check bodies, to keep lint time bounded). Add `"no-empty": ["error", { allowEmptyCatch: false }]` to the main rules block so a new bare `catch {}` has to be written as a commented no-op or a logged one.

findings.title: The admin alert webhook that every escalation path depends on defaults to empty and has no test-delivery path, so an operator cannot know it works until an incident
findings.description: sendAdminAlert (lib/admin/alert-webhook.ts:40-44) begins `const url = await getSetting("ADMIN_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL"); if (!url) return;` and the default is the empty string (lib/config/config-values.ts:429, registered at lib/config/registry.ts:2783). Every push signal in the app routes through it: the five worker escalators via lib/admin/failure-escalation.ts:100, and the boot-time schema, stale-scan and missing-table alerts at instrumentation.ts:139, :184, :198, :3491, :3531, :3631. Grepping ADMIN_ALERT_WEBHOOK across app/, components/ and lib/ finds only the config registry entries and alert-webhook.ts itself: there is no route, button, or admin action that sends a test alert, and the delivery failure paths (:50-56 for an unsafe URL, :86-90 for a non-2xx response) only console.error into a log the operator would have to already be reading.
findings.impact: An operator who pastes a Slack or PagerDuty URL into the setting has no way to confirm it works. A typo, a revoked Slack webhook, or a URL that validateScanTarget (:47) now rejects produces a silent no-op, and the first time they find out is the incident the alert existed for. Until it is configured at all, the app has no push signal of any kind, which is the state a fresh install ships in.
findings.recommendation: Add a "Send test alert" action next to the ADMIN_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL setting that calls sendAdminAlert with a `severity: "warning", event: "test_alert"` payload and surfaces the delivery result (including the non-2xx status from :87) in the UI rather than only in console.error. Have sendAdminAlert return a boolean instead of void so the caller can report it.

findings.title: Staff OIDC validates the ID token's issuer against the discovery document's own claim, not against the configured issuer URL
findings.description: verifyStaffOidcIdToken calls `jwtVerify(idToken, jwks, { issuer: doc.issuer, audience: config.clientId })` at lib/auth/staff-oidc.ts:127-130, where `doc` is whatever came back from `${STAFF_OIDC_ISSUER_URL}/.well-known/openid-configuration` (getDiscoveryDocument, line 64). `doc.issuer` is never compared against `config.issuerUrl`, and getDiscoveryDocument's own validation at lines 82-86 checks only that authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, and jwks_uri are present -- issuer is not in that list even though it is declared required on the DiscoveryDocument interface at line 51. OIDC Discovery 1.0 section 4.3 requires the returned `issuer` to exactly match the issuer used to build the discovery URL, precisely so this check is not circular. The rest of the flow is sound: the nonce is bound through a short-lived httpOnly cookie (app/api/v3/auth/staff-oidc/route.ts:168), state is HMAC-signed, and the callback never creates or promotes an account (callback lines 87-92).
findings.impact: No exploitable path today: reaching the vulnerable condition requires the admin-configured STAFF_OIDC_ISSUER_URL to serve a discovery document naming a different issuer and pointing jwks_uri at that issuer's keys, which means the admin already pointed staff SSO at a hostile endpoint. Worth fixing because it is the one place in an otherwise careful OIDC implementation where the trust anchor is self-asserted, and because the interface already declares the field required while the validation does not check it.
findings.recommendation: In lib/auth/staff-oidc.ts getDiscoveryDocument (line 82), add `doc.issuer` to the required-fields check and reject when `doc.issuer.replace(/\/+$/, "") !== base`, so the discovery document must self-identify as the issuer the admin configured before any of its endpoints are used.

findings.title: SQL, XSS, path-traversal, command-injection, deserialization and secret-exposure surfaces were swept clean this pass, so the next audit can skip re-deriving them
findings.category: injection surfaces verified clean (scope note, no action required)
findings.description:
Recorded so this ground is not re-walked. SQL: every pool.query interpolation site was opened. The only dynamic SQL fragments are whitelist-derived (app/api/v3/admin/features/route.ts:210-230 filters against an ALLOWED_COLUMNS Set; lib/auth/authorization.ts:292 derives both table and owner column from the OWNERSHIP map; app/api/v3/history/[id]/route.ts:339-357 and app/api/v3/schedules/route.ts:301-315 build SET clauses from server-side literals only; app/api/v3/ai/conversations/route.ts:155-178 and app/api/v3/admin/support-tickets/route.ts:35-45 build WHERE from validated enums). No dynamic ORDER BY, no `IN (${...})` list building, no string-concatenated table names. lib/domains/scope.ts:50 uses a DB value as a LIKE right-hand side, but lib/domains/verification.ts:45 constrains it to `^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$`.

XSS: only three dangerouslySetInnerHTML sites exist outside the scanner's own detection strings (components/ui/chart.tsx:82 config-derived, app/layout.tsx:158 a nonce'd bootstrap over JSON.stringify'd constants, components/seo/structured-data.tsx:57 through safeJsonLd's `<`/`>`/`&` escape). No innerHTML anywhere in extension/src. Every notification/scan-result href sink goes through safeHref (lib/ui/utils.ts:19). Emails escape scan data (lib/email/email.ts:1305, :1375, :1462, :1538). Markdown/compliance exports escape via lib/reports/md-escape.ts; the PDF writer escapes `\`, `(`, `)` at lib/reports/pdf-report.ts:51; SARIF is JSON.stringify.

Path traversal: avatars are BYTEA rows, not files (lib/uploads/avatar-storage.ts), and the upload path enforces a PNG/JPEG MIME plus magic-bytes allowlist (app/api/v3/auth/update/route.ts:255-290). app/api/v3/ai/context/route.ts:18-25 joins only fixed literal segments. app/api/v3/admin/backup/route.ts has no download-by-name. The updater extracts with `tar -xzf -C <tmp>` after checksum and cosign verification (lib/updater/apply.ts:178-189).

Command injection: the only child_process users are lib/updater/exec.ts, lib/backup/run-backup.ts and scripts/, all argv arrays with `shell: false`. No eval, new Function, vm, or request-derived dynamic import anywhere in app/, lib/, components/ or extension/src.

Prototype pollution: no recursive merge helper exists; the one `{...updates}` spread of a request body (app/api/v3/admin/features/route.ts:203) is filtered through an allowlist Set immediately after.

Secrets: no hardcoded credentials outside scanner test fixtures and docs placeholders; the only NEXT_PUBLIC_ vars hold an app URL, a Turnstile site key, a Stripe publishable key and SEO verification tokens; no token/secret/password value is passed to console.*; no route returns a secret column (lib/history/resolve-scan.ts:61 does `SELECT *` but every caller projects explicit fields).
findings.impact: None. This is a coverage record.
findings.recommendation: No action. If a future change adds a dynamic ORDER BY, a raw-HTML markdown renderer, a filesystem-backed upload path, or a recursive config merge, re-open the corresponding item above.

findings.title: checkRateLimit uses epoch-aligned fixed windows, so a caller gets up to 2x the cap across a bucket boundary
findings.description: lib/rate-limiting/rate-limit.ts:127-128 quantises the bucket to `Math.floor(now.getTime() / windowMs) * windowMs` and the UPSERT at :137-144 counts against `UNIQUE (key, window_start)`. This is a fixed window, not a sliding one, so a caller who spends the full cap in the last instant of one bucket and the full cap in the first instant of the next gets 2 x maxAttempts within one window's duration. For login that is 10 attempts inside 15 minutes rather than 5 (lib/config/config-values.ts:457-458); for demo scans, 10 anonymous scans inside a 12-hour span. The quantisation itself is deliberate and fixes a worse bug the comment at :120-126 describes (N requests in 1 ms creating N distinct buckets), so this is the residual, well-understood trade-off rather than a regression. Noted for the record: the limiter is correctly fail-CLOSED (a pool.query rejection propagates out of checkRateLimit and every caller's try/catch or withErrorHandling turns it into a 5xx, never an allowed request), the store is Postgres and therefore survives deploys and multiple instances, and getDailyRequestCount at lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts:157 reads `window_start >= CURRENT_DATE` while every writer uses `date_trunc('day', NOW())` -- consistent only while the database session timezone is UTC.
findings.impact: Doubles the effective burst on every named limit at bucket boundaries. Matters most for the login and 2FA-verify gates, where the per-account counters (`login-fail:${user.id}`) are the real defence and this is the outer layer.
findings.recommendation: If tightening is wanted, move checkRateLimit to a two-bucket weighted sliding window: read the current and previous bucket counts in the same statement and reject when `prev * (1 - elapsed/windowMs) + curr >= maxAttempts`. Otherwise document the 2x boundary behaviour next to the bucketStart comment so the shipped numbers are read as ceilings of 2x, and pin the database session to UTC so the CURRENT_DATE / date_trunc pair cannot diverge.

findings.title: next/font generates Inter and JetBrains Mono (13 woff2 files, 15 @font-face rules, a 4 KB stylesheet on every page) for fonts the site never applies
findings.description: app/layout.tsx:39-43 calls Inter() and JetBrains_Mono() and assigns them to `_inter` and `_jetbrainsMono`, which are never referenced; body uses `className="font-sans antialiased"` (line 170) and neither app/globals.css nor tailwind.config.mjs maps font-sans/font-mono to the --font-inter/--font-jetbrains-mono variables. The build still emits the pipeline: 13 woff2 files totalling ~305 KB under .next/static/media, and a 4 KB stylesheet (.next/static/css/51be877e094ecfa4.css) with 15 @font-face rules that is linked from the root layout on every page. .next/server/next-font-manifest.json is `{"pages":{},"app":{},"appUsingSizeAdjust":false}`, confirming no preload links are emitted and no size-adjust fallback metrics are generated, so the woff2 files are never actually downloaded -- only the stylesheet is. This is the performance side of AUDIT-011 design-02, which filed the same root cause as a branding issue; it is recorded here for the byte cost, not as a second fix.
findings.impact: Every page load fetches an extra render-blocking 4 KB stylesheet declaring fonts nothing uses, and the build ships 305 KB of dead font assets. The site renders in system-ui, which at least means no font-swap layout shift, but the whole next/font setup is cost with no benefit.
findings.recommendation: Pick one: either apply the fonts (add `${_inter.variable} ${_jetbrainsMono.variable}` to the html className in app/layout.tsx:149 and map font-sans/font-mono to those variables in tailwind.config.mjs, which also gets the size-adjust fallback metrics), or delete the two loader calls at app/layout.tsx:39-43 and the next/font/google import at line 4. Do not leave it half-wired.
